stops.note: meant 'bowstring', used for the trigonometric chord of an arc
Arab mathematicians phonetically transliterated the Sanskrit term
stops.meaning: chord of an arc (a meaningless transliteration in Arabic)

stops.note: later writers mistook 'jiba' for the real Arabic word 'jaib'
Gherardo of Cremona translated the Arabic word by its Latin equivalent
a Latin translator misread Arabic 'jiba' as 'jaib', fold or bay, and translated it 'sinus'

current_meaning: One of the three primary trigonometric functions, relating an angle of a right triangle to the ratio of its opposite side to the hypotenuse.
